crops.ps: 0-2 weeks before average last spring frost (CSU GardenNotes 720); Illinois Extension allows 2-3 weeks before
crops.pf: Illinois: potato is best planted in spring only
crops.clim: Cool-season crop grown nationwide; plant seed pieces 2-3 in deep (K-State).
crops.indr: Large plants; no extension indoor source covers potatoes (editorial).
crops.cons: 10–15 gallon container about 2–3 ft tall (UGA Extension)
crops.sto: Cure 14 days at 50-60°F, then store dark at 32-40°F and ~95% RH: about 6 months (UMN). Potatoes for frying: 40-50°F to avoid cold sweetening.
notes: Use certified seed potatoes; hill soil around stems so tubers stay covered (green skin contains solanine).

crops.ps: Plant slips after frost danger has passed and soil has warmed to 65°F (UMD); CSU very-tender class: 2+ weeks after last frost
crops.clim: Needs a long warm season: 85-120 frost-free growing days after soil reaches 65°F (UMD).
crops.indr: Sprawling vines; UMD covers only starting slips indoors (14-16 h grow lights).
crops.cons: 10-gallon container, one plant (University of Maryland Extension)
crops.sto: Cure ~85°F, 80-90% RH, 5-10 days (home: ~1 week in a warm covered spot); store at 55-60°F, 85-90% RH through winter (UMD). Do not refrigerate.
notes: Grow from slips (sprouts), not seed; harvest before frost and handle gently—skins bruise easily before curing.

crops.ps: 0-2 weeks before average last spring frost (CSU GardenNotes 720); Illinois Extension allows 2-3 weeks before
crops.pf: Fall crop: sow/transplant mid-July to early September (Illinois); or count back from the average first fall frost: days to harvest + transplant-raising days + harvest period + ~14-day "fall factor" (UNL NebGuide G1343)
crops.clim: Cool-season root crop; spring and fall crops.
crops.indr: Not listed among indoor crops (UT W1288-B); needs deep soil (editorial).
crops.cons: 5-gallon window box at least 12 in deep (UMaine #2762)
crops.sto: Remove tops; cold and moist (32-40°F, ~95% RH): about 8 months (UMN).
notes: Sow shallow (about 1/4-1/2 in) and keep the surface moist until seedlings emerge; thin to final spacing.

crops.ps: 0-2 weeks before average last spring frost (CSU GardenNotes 720); Illinois Extension allows 2-3 weeks before
crops.pf: Fall crop: sow/transplant mid-July to early September (Illinois); or count back from the average first fall frost: days to harvest + transplant-raising days + harvest period + ~14-day "fall factor" (UNL NebGuide G1343)
crops.clim: Cool-season; spring and fall crops.
crops.indr: Roots not listed as indoor crops (UT W1288-B); beet microgreens are possible (UMD).
crops.sto: Remove tops; cold and moist: about 5 months (UMN).
notes: Each beet "seed" is a cluster that sprouts several seedlings; thin early.

crops.ps: 0-2 weeks before average last spring frost (CSU GardenNotes 720); Illinois Extension allows 2-3 weeks before
crops.pf: Illinois: best planted in spring only
crops.clim: Long-season cool crop; roots can be harvested after light frost (UMN).
crops.sto: Cold and moist: about 4 months; sweetens after 2 weeks at 32°F (UMN).
notes: Germination is slow (10-21 days per K-State); keep seedbed moist.

crops.ps: 2-4 weeks before average last spring frost (CSU GardenNotes 720); Illinois Extension allows 4-6 weeks before
crops.pf: Fall crop: sow/transplant mid-July to early September (Illinois); or count back from the average first fall frost: days to harvest + transplant-raising days + harvest period + ~14-day "fall factor" (UNL NebGuide G1343)
crops.clim: Cool-season; rutabaga is better suited to a fall crop because of its long season (editorial inference from 90-120 days).
crops.indr: Root crop not covered for indoor growing.
crops.sto: Cold and moist: about 4 months (UMN, turnips and rutabagas).
notes: Turnip greens are a second harvest; rutabagas sweeten in cool fall weather.

crops.ps: 2-4 weeks before average last spring frost (CSU GardenNotes 720); Illinois Extension allows 4-6 weeks before
crops.clim: Bulbing depends on day length; choose short-, intermediate- or long-day types for your latitude (general extension guidance; ask local extension).
crops.indr: Bulb onions not covered indoors; onion microgreens/greens are possible (UMD).
crops.sto: Cure at room temperature 2-4 weeks, then cold and dry (32-40°F, ~65% RH): about 4 months (UMN). Do not freeze.
notes: Harvest when necks are tight and scales dry (UMN).

crops.pf: Plant cloves 2 in deep in fall (Illinois: best planted in fall; Ohio State: late fall). Fall plantings make larger bulbs than spring plantings (Ohio State).
crops.clim: Hardneck (rocambole) types do poorly in warmer climates; softnecks store longer (Ohio State).
crops.sto: Ohio State: cure 2-3 weeks (above freezing to 40°F, RH ≤75%); WSU: store cold and dry, 32-50°F, 60-70% RH. Use net bags, not plastic.
notes: Do not plant grocery-store garlic; buy seed garlic adapted to your area (Ohio State).
Remove hardneck scapes for larger bulbs (Ohio State).

crops.ps: 2 or more weeks after average last spring frost (CSU GardenNotes 720)
crops.clim: Needs warm soil (75-85°F optimum germination, K-State) and a frost-free season of about 3+ months.
crops.sto: Cool and dry (50-60°F, ~60% RH): 2-6 months depending on type (UMN). Do not cure Table Queen/acorn types.
notes: Harvest when the rind is hard and before frost; leave a stem attached.

crops.ps: 2 or more weeks after average last spring frost (CSU GardenNotes 720)
crops.clim: Long warm season; large vines.
crops.sto: Cool and dry: about 2 months; sensitive below 45°F (UMN).
notes: Pie (small sugar) types are better eating than large carving types (general guidance).

crops.ps: around the average last spring frost date, from seed (CSU GardenNotes 720); transplants without protection wait until frost risk passes
crops.pf: For a late planting, count back from first fall frost: days to harvest + 14-day fall factor + 14-day frost-tender factor (UNL G1343)
crops.clim: Warm-season; quick to bear.
crops.sto: About 1 week at ~55°F in perforated bags; no more than 4 days in refrigerator (UMN).
notes: Pick at 4-6 in long (UMN) every day or two; plants slow down if fruit is left to grow large.

crops.ps: After last frost when soil is at least 50°F, germinates quickly above 60°F (WSU); CSU tender class: around last frost
crops.clim: Needs 90-120 days to dry on the plant; WSU protein about 22%.
crops.indr: Low yield per area; outdoor field crop.
crops.sto: Thresh and store in a tightly closed container in a dark, dry place; keeps several years, but after 3+ years may develop "hard seed" (WSU).
notes: Very low yield per square foot but a calorie- and protein-dense, shelf-stable food.
Never eat raw dry beans; cook thoroughly (general food safety).

crops.ps: around the average last spring frost date, from seed (CSU GardenNotes 720)
crops.pf: For a late planting, count back from first fall frost: days to harvest + 14-day fall factor + 14-day frost-tender factor (UNL G1343)
crops.clim: Warm-season; succession sow for continuous harvest.
crops.sto: Cold and moist about 1 week; pitting below 40°F (UMN).
notes: Pick pods before seeds bulge, 2-3 weeks after bloom (UMN); frequent picking keeps plants bearing.

crops.ps: 2-4 weeks before average last spring frost (CSU GardenNotes 720); Illinois Extension allows 4-6 weeks before
crops.clim: Cool-season; production drops in hot weather.
crops.indr: Pea shoots/microgreens are listed by UMD; full pea plants are not covered indoors.
crops.sto: Cold and moist about 1 week (UMN).
notes: Provide a trellis for tall varieties.

crops.pf: Texas A&M: seed in the fall for an early spring crop (mild-winter areas). Cold-winter timing not verified.
crops.clim: Cool-season legume.
notes: Some people with G6PD deficiency react to fava beans (favism); a well-established medical caution.

crops.ps: around the average last spring frost date, from seed (CSU GardenNotes 720)
crops.clim: Plant in blocks of several short rows rather than one long row for wind pollination (general extension practice).
crops.sto: Cold and moist about 5 days (UMN); best eaten soon after picking.
notes: Harvest when silks are dry and brown and kernels are milky (UMN).
Keep sweet corn isolated from field/popcorn (UACES: 500 ft or 14 days apart).

crops.ps: around the average last spring frost date, from seed (CSU GardenNotes 720)
crops.clim: Needs to reach physiological maturity before fall frost (UVM). Isolate from sweet corn: 500 ft or 14 days apart (UACES).
crops.sto: Dry ears, shell, then treat for insects (hold at 120°F core for 30 min, or freeze 4 days at 0°F) and store airtight (UACES). 1 lb shelled corn yields about 1 lb meal.
notes: Leave ears on stalks to dry as long as wildlife allows; shell only when dry (UACES).

crops.n: Cowpeas / Southern peas (black-eyed, crowder, purple hull)
crops.ps: After soil is thoroughly warm, at least 60-62°F (Clemson, U. Arkansas)
crops.pf: About 65-75 days before the average first fall frost (U. Arkansas)
crops.clim: Heat-loving; produces under harsh conditions (Clemson).
crops.sto: Fresh pods: shade quickly and shell/process rapidly (Clemson). Dry seeds: no storage guidance found in sources checked.
notes: Very drought- and heat-tolerant protein crop for hot summers.

crops.ps: Around last frost when soil is above 65°F (USU)
crops.clim: Grow only where the frost-free season exceeds 110 days (USU); Valencia types suit shorter seasons.
crops.sto: Dry ~4 weeks total; store at 35-40°F and 50-60% RH. Roasted: 3-4 weeks at room temperature, 6-12 months refrigerated, 1+ year frozen (USU).
notes: Light sandy soil; hill soil around plants when about 1 ft tall (USU).

crops.ps: After last threat of frost (WVU)
crops.clim: Warm-season.
notes: Harvest when the back of the head turns brown (WVU); cover heads to protect seeds from birds (general practice).

crops.ps: 2 or more weeks after average last spring frost (CSU GardenNotes 720) (transplants; start seed indoors 4-8 weeks earlier per K-State)
crops.clim: Warm-season; fruit set suffers in very hot or cool nights (K-State: blossom drop).
crops.indr: UT: compact tomatoes can grow under lights but likely need supplemental light all year (2,400 fc at 16 h).
crops.sto: About 5 days at ~55°F; do not refrigerate (UMN).
notes: Stake or cage plants; mulch and water evenly to reduce blossom-end rot (K-State).

crops.ps: 2 or more weeks after average last spring frost (CSU GardenNotes 720)
crops.clim: As tomatoes.
crops.indr: UT: compact tomatoes under lights (2,400 fc at 16 h/day).
crops.sto: About 5 days at ~55°F; do not refrigerate (UMN, tomatoes).
notes: Higher yield by weight than slicers in the LSU table; good for containers.

crops.ps: 2 or more weeks after average last spring frost (CSU GardenNotes 720) (transplants started 6-8 weeks earlier, CSU)
crops.clim: Warm-season; slow from seed.
crops.indr: Fruiting crops need much more light indoors (UT W1288-B); peppers not specifically listed.
crops.sto: About 2 weeks at ~55°F; pitting below 45°F (UMN).
notes: Letting peppers ripen to red raises vitamin C and A (FDC red vs green values).

crops.ps: 2 or more weeks after average last spring frost (CSU GardenNotes 720)
crops.clim: Needs heat; very tender.
crops.sto: About 1 week at ~55°F; chilling injury below 50°F (UMN).
notes: Harvest before the skin loses its gloss (UMN).

crops.ps: around the average last spring frost date, from seed (CSU GardenNotes 720); unprotected transplants after frost risk passes
crops.pf: For a late planting, count back from first fall frost: days to harvest + 14-day fall factor + 14-day frost-tender factor (UNL G1343)
crops.clim: Trellising saves space (Cornell trellised spacing is much tighter).
crops.indr: Fruiting vine needing high light; not covered indoors.
crops.sto: About 1 week at ~55°F in perforated bags; chilling injury below 40°F; keep away from apples and tomatoes (UMN).
notes: Pick slicers at about 6 in (UMN) and keep picking so vines keep producing.

crops.ps: 2-4 weeks before average last spring frost (CSU GardenNotes 720); Illinois Extension allows 4-6 weeks before
crops.pf: Fall crop: sow/transplant mid-July to early September (Illinois); or count back from the average first fall frost: days to harvest + transplant-raising days + harvest period + ~14-day "fall factor" (UNL NebGuide G1343)
crops.clim: Cool-season; flavor improves after frost (general extension guidance).
crops.indr: Leafy greens are among the easiest indoor crops (UT W1288-B); kale is a common microgreen (UMD). Needs 4-6 h sun or grow lights.
notes: Harvest lower leaves first and let the plant keep growing.

crops.ps: 2-4 weeks before average last spring frost (CSU GardenNotes 720); Illinois Extension allows 4-6 weeks before
crops.pf: Fall crop: sow/transplant mid-July to early September (Illinois); or count back from the average first fall frost: days to harvest + transplant-raising days + harvest period + ~14-day "fall factor" (UNL NebGuide G1343)
crops.clim: Tolerates heat better than most greens and is a Southern fall/winter staple (LSU yield is from the Deep South).
crops.indr: Leafy green (UT W1288-B), but large plants.
notes: Harvest outer leaves over a long season.

crops.ps: 0-2 weeks before average last spring frost (CSU GardenNotes 720); Illinois Extension allows 2-3 weeks before
crops.pf: Fall crop: sow/transplant mid-July to early September (Illinois); or count back from the average first fall frost: days to harvest + transplant-raising days + harvest period + ~14-day "fall factor" (UNL NebGuide G1343)
crops.clim: Tolerates summer heat better than spinach and lettuce; harvest over a long season.
crops.indr: Leafy greens are among the easiest indoor crops (UT W1288-B); chard is listed as a microgreen (UMD).
notes: Cut outer leaves repeatedly; plants regrow from the center.

crops.ps: 2-4 weeks before average last spring frost (CSU GardenNotes 720); Illinois Extension allows 4-6 weeks before
crops.pf: Fall crop: sow/transplant mid-July to early September (Illinois); or count back from the average first fall frost: days to harvest + transplant-raising days + harvest period + ~14-day "fall factor" (UNL NebGuide G1343)
crops.clim: Bolts in long, hot days; best in spring and fall.
crops.indr: Leafy green (UT W1288-B); 4-6 h sun or grow lights.
crops.sto: Cold and moist about 10 days (UMN).
notes: Sow every 2 weeks in cool weather for a steady supply.

crops.ps: 0-2 weeks before average last spring frost (CSU GardenNotes 720); Illinois Extension allows 2-3 weeks before
crops.pf: Fall crop: sow/transplant mid-July to early September (Illinois); or count back from the average first fall frost: days to harvest + transplant-raising days + harvest period + ~14-day "fall factor" (UNL NebGuide G1343)
crops.clim: Bolts and turns bitter in heat; light summer shade may help (Missouri).
crops.indr: Leafy greens are the easiest indoor crops; lettuce tolerates lower light (UT W1288-B, UMD).
crops.sto: Cold and moist about 1 week (UMN).
notes: Cut-and-come-again leaf types give several harvests.

crops.ps: 2-4 weeks before average last spring frost (CSU GardenNotes 720); Illinois Extension allows 4-6 weeks before (transplants)
crops.pf: Fall crop: sow/transplant mid-July to early September (Illinois); or count back from the average first fall frost: days to harvest + transplant-raising days + harvest period + ~14-day "fall factor" (UNL NebGuide G1343); CSU: direct-seed early July (Front Range)
crops.clim: Cool-season; spring and fall crops.
crops.indr: Large heads; not covered indoors (cabbage microgreens are possible, UMD).
crops.sto: Cold and moist: about 5 months (UMN).
notes: Harvest when heads are compact and firm (UMN).

crops.ps: 2-4 weeks before average last spring frost (CSU GardenNotes 720); Illinois Extension allows 4-6 weeks before (transplants)
crops.pf: Fall crop: sow/transplant mid-July to early September (Illinois); or count back from the average first fall frost: days to harvest + transplant-raising days + harvest period + ~14-day "fall factor" (UNL NebGuide G1343); CSU: direct-seed early July (Front Range)
crops.clim: Cool-season; heads loosen in heat.
crops.indr: Large plants (broccoli microgreens are common, UMD).
crops.sto: Cold and moist about 2 weeks (UMN).
notes: Harvest while buds are tight; side shoots follow (UMN).

crops.ps: 2-4 weeks before average last spring frost (CSU GardenNotes 720); Illinois Extension allows 4-6 weeks before
crops.pf: Fall crop: sow/transplant mid-July to early September (Illinois); or count back from the average first fall frost: days to harvest + transplant-raising days + harvest period + ~14-day "fall factor" (UNL NebGuide G1343)
crops.clim: Fastest root crop; bolts in heat.
crops.indr: Radish is a standard microgreen (UMD); full roots not covered indoors.
crops.sto: Remove tops; cold and moist about 1 month (UMN).
notes: Sow small amounts every 1-2 weeks; harvest before roots exceed about 1-1/4 in (UMN).

crops.ps: Year-round indoors
crops.pf: Year-round indoors
crops.clim: Indoor crop: about 16 h of light per day, lights 6-12 in above foliage, 70-75°F (UMD).
crops.indr: Quickest crop with the lowest light needs (UT W1288-B; UMD).
crops.cons: Shallow tray, e.g., standard 10 x 20 in flat with 1-1.5 in of medium (UMD)
crops.sto: Rinse, pat dry, refrigerate up to 10 days (UMD).
notes: Good crops: radish, broccoli, kale, mustard, arugula, beet, chard, peas, sunflower (UMD).

crops.ps: Basil: treat as tender (after frost); parsley/cilantro: cool season - not verified per herb
crops.clim: Perennial herbs (thyme, oregano, rosemary) not covered here.
crops.indr: Herbs and leafy greens are the easiest indoor crops; need 4-6 h direct sun or grow lights (basil 1,400 fc at 16 h) (UT W1288-B).
crops.cons: Small to medium containers (UT W1288-B; no size given)
crops.sto: Basil: room temperature with stems in water, about 5 days; discolors in the refrigerator (UMN).
notes: Pinch basil tips to keep plants bushy (general practice).

crops.ps: Early spring (Kansas: February-April per K-State MF352)
crops.clim: Grown nationwide; June-bearing in matted rows, everbearing/day-neutral for longer harvest. LSU yield reflects Southern annual production.
crops.indr: UT: strawberries can grow in containers under lights (2,000 fc at 16 h/day).
notes: Mulch beds for winter in cold areas (K-State: late November/December in Kansas).

crops.ps: Early spring (K-State MF352 planting window Feb-Apr in Kansas)
crops.znote: Northern highbush flower buds injured below -20°F (Ohio State) - about the zone 5 minimum (derived from USDA zone bands). Half-high types tolerate -35 to -45°F. Rabbiteye and southern highbush are for the South (Ohio State lists the types; no zone figures).
crops.clim: Needs acid soil, pH 4.5-5.2 (Ohio State); amend with sulfur well before planting.
notes: Plant two or more cultivars for bigger berries and yields (Ohio State).
Net plants against birds.

crops.ps: Early spring (K-State MF352)
crops.znote: No zone figures in sources checked; K-State rates raspberries hardy, blackberries moderately hardy.
crops.clim: Brambles tolerate a little shade (K-State).
notes: Remove fruited (floricane) canes after harvest; trellis for easier care.

crops.ps: Early spring (K-State MF352)
crops.znote: Iowa State: some cultivars are rated hardy to -30°F (about zone 4) in Minnesota but only to about -20°F where winters are milder. Cultivar choice matters.
crops.clim: Needs lots of sun and good air flow.
notes: Prune hard every dormant season (K-State).

crops.ps: Early spring crowns (K-State calendar)
crops.znote: UMN: hardy in zone 4, worth trying in zone 3
crops.clim: Needs winter cold.
crops.sto: Can be frozen (UMN).
notes: Never eat the leaves; stalks are high in oxalic acid (UMN).

crops.ps: Early spring crowns in trenches 6-12 in deep (UMN)
crops.znote: UMN: Jersey types can be damaged at -30°F without snow cover; Mary Washington very cold-hardy.
crops.clim: Long-lived bed; pick a permanent site.
crops.sto: Cold and moist, upright, about 2 weeks (UMN).
notes: Stop harvesting by about July 1 to let ferns rebuild the crowns (UMN).

crops.ps: 2 or more weeks after average last spring frost (CSU GardenNotes 720)
crops.clim: Needs heat; germination optimum 75-85°F (K-State).
crops.sto: Cold and moist about 1 week (UMN).
notes: Harvest when the fruit slips easily from the vine (UMN).

crops.ps: 2 or more weeks after average last spring frost (CSU GardenNotes 720)
crops.clim: Needs a long hot season; germination optimum 80-90°F (K-State).
crops.sto: About 2 weeks at ~55°F; decays below 50°F after a few days (UMN).
notes: Ripe when the ground spot turns yellow (UMN). High yield by weight but low in calories.

crops.ps: As early in spring as possible (Oregon: by May 15)
crops.znote: No zone figures in sources checked.
crops.clim: Tall (sunflower relative); spreads from leftover tubers—give it a contained spot.
crops.sto: 31-32°F and 90-95% RH: 4-5 months (Oregon State), with up to ~20% loss by 5 months.
notes: Inulin-rich tubers can cause gas in some people (general nutrition knowledge).

crops.ps: Early spring, dormant trees (K-State MF352)
crops.znote: UMaine: among the most winter-hardy fruits; varieties listed for zones 3-4. Warm-zone limit depends on chill hours (not verified here).
crops.clim: Most cultivars need a pollenizer variety (Oregon State; K-State "partially self-fruitful").
crops.sto: Cold and moist (32-40°F, 80-90% RH) per WSU; months vary by variety.
notes: Expect regular pest management (codling moth, scab) for clean fruit (Oregon State).

crops.ps: Early spring (K-State MF352)
crops.znote: UMaine: European pears zone 4 varieties; Asian pears hardy into zone 5.
crops.clim: Needs a second variety for pollination (K-State "self-sterile"); tolerates heavier soil better than other fruits (K-State).
notes: Fire blight is the main disease risk; choose resistant cultivars (Oregon State lists fire blight).

crops.ps: Early spring (K-State MF352)
crops.znote: UMaine: generally adapted to zone 6, some varieties in zone 5. Iowa State: some bud loss at -13 to -18°F; wood damage near -20°F.
crops.clim: Self-fruitful (K-State). Spring frosts often kill blossoms in marginal areas.
crops.indr: Tree (genetic dwarf peaches can be grown in pots and moved indoors in winter per Oregon State).
notes: Requires a disease/pest program (leaf curl, brown rot, borers) per Oregon State.

crops.ps: Early spring (K-State MF352)
crops.znote: UMaine: some Japanese plums zone 4 (possibly 3), European plums mostly zone 5; tart cherries zone 5 (a few southern zone 4); sweet cherries zone 5 but blossoms often frosted.
crops.clim: Tart cherries are self-fruitful and naturally semi-dwarf; sweet cherries usually need a pollenizer (K-State, UMaine).
notes: Plant Japanese plums with other Japanese plums for pollination (UMaine).

crops.ps: Spring
crops.znote: UT rates cultivars zone 6, 7 or 8; Celeste hardy to about 0°F, Brown Turkey about 10°F. Zone 6 only with protected sites/dieback (UT).
crops.clim: Warm, south-facing sites near walls improve survival (UT).
crops.indr: Containers can be moved into a garage when temperatures fall below 15-20°F (UT).
crops.cons: 20+ gallons for mature productive plants (UT D 234-B)
crops.sto: Short shelf life; refrigerated about 1 week, possibly 2 (UT).
notes: Figs need no pollenizer (Oregon State) and few sprays.

crops.ps: Container-grown trees can be planted any time of year (UF/IFAS)
crops.znote: Derived: Clemson minimum temperatures fall in zone 8b (15-20°F) to 9a (20-25°F) for the hardiest types (kumquat, satsuma); most citrus suits zones 9-11. Protect trees in 8b.
crops.clim: Limited to areas without regular freezes (UF/IFAS); satsumas are best for colder edges.
crops.indr: Not covered indoors in sources checked.
crops.sto: Fruit holds on the tree: satsuma 4-6 weeks; grapefruit over an extended period (UF/IFAS).
notes: Check citrus-greening quarantines before moving trees (Clemson).

crops.ps: Dormant season, December-February in Mississippi
crops.znote: No zone figures in sources checked; a Southern nut crop needing a long season.
crops.clim: Very large tree; plant at least two cultivars (common extension advice, not verified here).
notes: Optional crop for large lots and farms.

crops.ps: Dormant season / early spring
crops.znote: No zone figures in sources checked.
crops.clim: Needs a pollenizer cultivar; Eastern filbert blight is a major disease (Oregon State).
notes: Smaller than walnuts and pecans; a better fit for home lots.

crops.ps: Warm months
crops.znote: Derived from UF/IFAS cold-damage temperatures vs USDA zone bands: Mexican types to about zone 9a, others 9b-11.
crops.clim: Will not tolerate flooding or poorly drained soil (UF/IFAS).
crops.sto: Fruit ripens off the tree in 3-8 days at 60-75°F; ripe fruit can be refrigerated (UF/IFAS).
notes: Very high in calories and healthy fats compared with other fruit (FDC).

kcal.text: Adult estimated calorie needs range from 1,600 to 2,400 calories per day for females and 2,000 to 3,000 for males (DGA 2020-2025, Appendix 2, p. 139; based on IOM EER equations, reference man 5 ft 10 in/154 lb, woman 5 ft 4 in/126 lb). The current DGA 2025-2030 (Jan 2026) gives no ranges; it uses a 2,000-calorie reference pattern and says needs depend on age, sex, height, weight and activity.
